rules.statement: Fetch any URL supplied by a client or caller through a dedicated named HttpClient whose SocketsHttpHandler ConnectCallback resolves the host once, refuses loopback, private (RFC 1918), CGNAT, link-local, unique-local, multicast and reserved ranges (IPv4, IPv6 and IPv4-mapped IPv6), and connects the socket to the vetted IP. Do not use the shared default HttpClient for this.
rules.why: A server-side fetch of a caller-supplied URL is an SSRF sink. Resolving the address and pinning the socket to it is the only reliable defense against internal targets and DNS rebinding.
rules.check: Look for outbound requests to client-supplied or registration-supplied URLs that go through IHttpClientFactory's default client or a plain HttpClient, with no ConnectCallback that resolves the address, blocks private and reserved IPs, and connects to the resolved address.

rules.statement: Block private and internal targets by checking the resolved IP address at connect time, not by inspecting the URL's host string.
rules.why: A hostname can resolve to a private address (DNS rebinding), and IP literals can be obfuscated, so string checks on the host can be bypassed.
rules.check: Flag SSRF protections that compare Uri.Host against hostnames, IP-literal patterns or regexes and never check the address the socket actually connects to.

rules.statement: Set AllowAutoRedirect = false on HTTP handlers that fetch untrusted URLs.
rules.why: Following a redirect could send the guarded fetch on to an internal host.
rules.check: Look for SSRF-guarded or untrusted-URL handlers or clients that leave AllowAutoRedirect at its default of true.

rules.statement: Do not make the private-address SSRF block a setting that can be turned off. A deployment that has to reach non-public hosts should replace the whole fetching service instead.
rules.why: The block is the non-negotiable SSRF floor, and replacing the service keeps the secure default intact.
rules.check: Flag options or settings that disable the private or internal address block on an outbound fetch of untrusted URLs.

rules.statement: Bound outbound fetches of untrusted URLs with a configurable timeout, using a CancellationTokenSource linked to the caller's token, and report a timeout as a validation error that is distinct from caller cancellation.
rules.why: Without a timeout, a slow remote host can tie up the server. Separating the two cases makes sure a timeout is not mistaken for the caller cancelling.
rules.check: Look for untrusted outbound fetches with no timeout, with a timeout that is not linked to the caller's token, or that catch OperationCanceledException without checking whether the caller's token was the one cancelled.

rules.statement: Cap the response size of untrusted outbound fetches in two places: reject based on the advertised Content-Length, and enforce a hard byte limit while streaming the body.
rules.why: A Content-Length that lies or is missing must not be able to exhaust memory.
rules.check: Flag code that reads an untrusted response with ReadAsStringAsync or ReadAsByteArrayAsync and no limit, or that trusts Content-Length alone without counting bytes while reading.

rules.statement: Register replaceable extension-point services with TryAdd* (for example TryAddSingleton) so a deployment can override them through DI.
rules.why: Deployments with a different retrieval or trust model can then supply their own implementation without changing the endpoint.
rules.check: Look for default implementations of extension-point interfaces registered with AddSingleton or AddScoped instead of TryAdd*.

rules.statement: Keep synchronous metadata validation limited to cheap, pure checks, and move network-dependent validation behind a separate async, replaceable service.
rules.why: Isolating the remote step keeps the pure validation simple and lets the network policy be replaced.
rules.check: Flag network I/O, or sync-over-async calls, added inside synchronous metadata validation methods.

rules.statement: When validating a sector_identifier_uri at client registration and update, require an absolute https URI, require the fetched document to be a JSON array of strings, and require every registered redirect_uri to appear in that array using ordinal comparison. On failure, return invalid_client_metadata.
rules.why: OpenID Connect Core §8.1 requires this check so that clients can share a pairwise sector only when the party controlling the document vouches for their redirect URIs.
rules.check: Look for sector_identifier_uri handling that accepts non-https URIs, skips the fetch, accepts non-array or non-string JSON, uses case-insensitive or prefix matching, or misses redirect URIs on update.

rules.statement: Reject the dynamic registration of a pairwise client whose redirect_uris span more than one host if it does not supply a sector_identifier_uri.
rules.why: OpenID Connect Core §8.1 requires this because otherwise the client's sector is ambiguous.
rules.check: Look for registration validation that accepts subject_type=pairwise with redirect URIs on multiple hosts and no sector_identifier_uri.
